What is the infimum of the function $y=f(x)$ shown above?

${inf}_{x\in R}f(x)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The infimum of a function is the infimum of the range of the function.

In this case, the range of $f$ is $A=[-2,2].$

To find the infimum of a set $A,$ we must find the set containing **all** lower bounds of $A$ (i.e., the set of lower bounds) and take the maximum of this set.

So, in our case, we have that

- any number $y\le -2$ is a lower bound of $A,$

- any number $y>-2$ is **not** a lower bound of $A$ because $-2,$ an element of $A,$ is smaller than $y.$

Therefore, $(-\infty ,-2]$ is the set of lower bounds of $A,$ and

$$
{inf}_{x\in R}f(x)=inf(A)=max(-\infty ,-2]=-2.
$$
